[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended intermediate-level poses to improve flexibility:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Hanumanasana (Monkey Pose) - A deep hip opener that stretches the hamstrings, glutes, and hip flexors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Eka Pada Rajakapotasana (One-Legged King Pigeon Pose) - Stretches the hips, glutes, and lower back.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Prasarita Padottanasana (Wide-Legged Forward Fold) - Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and spine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended balance poses:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Vrksasana (Tree Pose) - Improves balance and stability.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Eagle Pose (Garudasana) - Challenges balance and strengthens ankles.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Astavakrasana (Eight-Angle Pose) - Improves balance, strength, and flexibility.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended other challenging poses:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Parivrtta Trikonasana (Revolved Triangle Pose) - Stretches the hips, thighs, and spine, while challenging balance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Bakasana (Crow Pose) - Strengthens arms and core, and improves balance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided tips for mastering Vrksasana (Tree Pose):  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Establish a strong foundation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Engage your core.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Focus on your drishti (gaze).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Relax your upper body.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Play with weight distribution.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Breathe and relax.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Practice variations and progressions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Listed common mistakes to avoid in Tree Pose.
